title: Release Checklist — SDK Parity (Auth/Retry/Timeout/Streaming)
content:
Owner: Connor O’Brien (Release coordination)
DRI: Monica Patel (SDK Engineering)
Tech lead: Ibrahim Khan

Purpose
This checklist is the release gate for shipping standardized SDK behavior across Python/TypeScript/Go for:
- Auth resolution + secret handling
- Retry policy (retryable errors, backoff/jitter, Retry-After)
- Timeout model (overall vs connect/read mapping)
- Streaming semantics (disconnects, partial output, cancellation, retry guidance)
- Typed errors + request_id propagation
- Telemetry/logging fields (or hooks) for debugging

This is meant to be pragmatic. If we can’t check an item, we must (a) document the gap in migration notes and (b) explicitly accept the risk in ENG-5131 with SRE/Security signoff.


A) Pre-release readiness (cross-language)
[ ] Parity matrix updated and marked “Release Candidate” for all rows in scope.
    - Matrix: sdk-parity-matrix-auth-retry-timeouts-streaming
    - All remaining “known mismatches” have either fixes merged or documented exceptions with rationale.

[ ] Standards/ADRs are final (no more behavioral churn expected for v1):
    - Retry/timeout standard published (SRE signoff).
    - Auth resolution + secret handling guidance published (Security signoff).
    - Timeout model ADR published.

[ ] Conformance test suite green for all three SDKs on main branch.
    - Includes: 429 + Retry-After cases, 5xx, network failures, timeout behavior, request_id propagation, streaming disconnect error shape.

[ ] Platform prerequisites confirmed shipped (or explicitly not required):
    - API gateway emits Retry-After on 429.
    - request_id consistently present on error responses (streaming + non-streaming).
    - error code enum stable for SDK classification.

[ ] Telemetry/logging schema aligned (minimum):
    - request_id
    - retry_count (attempt index and total attempts if available)
    - timeout_ms (overall, plus connect/read if supported)
    - streaming_disconnect_reason (best-effort; do not log secrets)

[ ] Support is ready:
    - ENG-5132 support playbook drafted and reviewed by Dev Patel / Owen Phillips.
    - Support macro includes: “SDK version”, “request_id”, “timeout config”, “retry config”, “streaming vs non-streaming”.


B) Versioning + packaging decisions
Goal: minimize breaking changes; when unavoidable, clearly flag and document.

[ ] Choose release line per SDK (fill in here before tagging):
    - Python: v___.___
    - TypeScript: v___.___
    - Go: v___.___

[ ] Semver check (per language norms):
    - Default behavior change that may alter retry volume/timeouts: treat as MINOR if backward compatible in API surface but behavior changes; MAJOR only if config names or call patterns break.
    - If any breaking behavior is unavoidable, confirm:
        [ ] migration notes explicitly call it out
        [ ] deprecation window documented (if applicable)
        [ ] opt-in flag exists where feasible

[ ] Dependency audit (avoid surprise upgrades):
    - Python: http client + extras pinned appropriately; no accidental major bump.
    - TS: fetch/polyfill expectations documented; Node version compatibility checked.
    - Go: module versions tidy; no incompatible context changes.

[ ] Release branch policy:
    - Decide whether we tag from main or cut release branches per repo.
    - Confirm the exact commit SHAs to tag are recorded in ENG-5131.


C) Changelog + migration notes (must be consistent)
[ ] Changelog entry added in each repo with the same structure and terms.
    Required bullets:
    - Auth: env var precedence + deprecations (old env vars, if any)
    - Retries: retryable codes + network errors; Retry-After respected; default max attempts
    - Timeouts: new default(s) + how to configure overall/connect/read
    - Streaming: disconnect behavior + partial output semantics + cancellation notes
    - Errors: typed error taxonomy; request_id now present everywhere
    - Observability: logging/telemetry fields (or hooks)

[ ] Migration guide updated and linked from each changelog.
    - Docs: sdk-migration-notes-auth-retry-timeout
    - Include copy/paste snippets for Python/TS/Go using the same option names where possible.

[ ] Deprecation messaging:
    - If old env vars or config keys are still supported:
        [ ] they emit a deprecation warning (non-spammy; once per process)
        [ ] deprecation removal timeline is stated

[ ] Examples/quickstarts updated:
    - streaming quickstart uses the standardized semantics + shows recommended timeouts.
    - quickstarts show explicit retry configuration (even if defaults are acceptable) so users learn the knobs.


D) Security + privacy gates
[ ] Secret redaction verified:
    - API keys/tokens never appear in logs/errors.
    - Debug logging does not print Authorization header.
    - Error messages mention “missing/invalid credentials” without echoing values.

[ ] Auth precedence confirmed across SDKs:
    - Explicit constructor/config parameter wins over env var.
    - Canonical env var names confirmed (and any legacy names documented + deprecated).

[ ] Security review signoff recorded (Marcus Lin or delegate) for:
    - auth defaults
    - error messages + redaction
    - telemetry fields (no sensitive payloads)


E) Reliability / SRE gates
[ ] Retry defaults reviewed with SRE (Allison Grant / Sean Gallagher):
    - max attempts
    - backoff base + cap
    - jitter strategy
    - Retry-After parsing behavior (seconds + date formats)
    - retry budget guidance (docs)

[ ] Thundering herd safeguards:
    - backoff includes jitter
    - respects Retry-After
    - no retries on 4xx except 408/409/429 as per standard

[ ] Streaming retry posture is conservative and documented:
    - No automatic retry once streaming tokens have been delivered unless caller opts in.
    - Docs explicitly warn about potential duplicate side effects.
    - Idempotency guidance included (how to use idempotency keys / request IDs).

[ ] Observability dashboards ready (or at minimum queries saved):
    - retry rate by SDK + version
    - 429 rate and Retry-After compliance proxy
    - timeout rate
    - streaming disconnect reasons
    - request_id presence rate in errors

[ ] Rollback triggers agreed (write into ENG-5131):
    - retry rate spikes above X% over baseline
    - 429s or 5xx increase correlated with new SDK versions
    - streaming disconnects up materially
    - support escalations exceed threshold


F) CI / build / publication gates (per repo)
Python
[ ] All tests green including conformance fixtures on CI.
[ ] Build artifacts validated locally (sdist/wheel).
[ ] “Requests vs httpx” (or chosen client) timeout mapping verified in at least one integration test.
[ ] PyPI publish checklist done:
    - version bumped
    - changelog updated
    - tags pushed

TypeScript
[ ] All tests green including conformance fixtures.
[ ] Bundling validated (ESM/CJS as applicable) + tree-shaking sanity check.
[ ] AbortController behavior verified for:
    - non-streaming request timeout
    - streaming cancellation
[ ] npm publish checklist done:
    - version bumped
    - changelog updated
    - tags pushed

Go
[ ] All tests green including conformance fixtures.
[ ] Context cancellation verified aborts HTTP + streaming reads.
[ ] go mod tidy clean; tag triggers module version correctly.


G) Canary + rollout plan
[ ] Identify canary users (internal + friendly external).
    Internal dogfood targets:
    - Redwood Console / internal tools calling hosted API
    - at least one service behind a proxy (to exercise streaming failure modes)

[ ] External canary list confirmed with PM/CS (no surprises):
    - 3–5 customers who previously hit 429/timeouts/streaming disconnects.
    - Prefer customers with strong observability and willingness to share request_ids.

[ ] Canary instructions prepared (single doc/README snippet):
    - how to upgrade
    - recommended default config
    - what to log (request_id, SDK version)
    - how to report issues + where (Linear issue template)

[ ] Rollout phases (suggested):
    Phase 0: Internal only (24–48h)
    Phase 1: External beta tag/channel (3–7 days)
    Phase 2: Stable release across all repos within 48h window

[ ] Coordinated timing across SDKs:
    - Target to avoid “TS has it but Python doesn’t” window longer than 2 business days.
    - If a repo slips, we must pin docs to “coming soon” for that language.


H) Validation steps (post-release)
Within 2 hours of publish
[ ] Confirm packages available:
    - PyPI / npm / Go module proxy
[ ] Smoke test each SDK against hosted API:
    - basic request
    - forced 429 scenario (or fixture endpoint) validates Retry-After behavior
    - forced timeout scenario (small timeout) surfaces typed Timeout error
    - streaming request cancel/disconnect yields expected error shape

Within 24–72 hours
[ ] Monitor dashboards for regression.
[ ] Check support queue for spikes; ensure macros are used.
[ ] Validate request_id presence in real customer-reported errors.

Within 1 week
[ ] Adoption snapshot:
    - percentage of requests by SDK version (where visible)
    - top errors by code/status
    - retry distribution (attempt counts)


I) Release comms checklist
[ ] #eng-releases post includes:
    - versions for all three SDKs
    - link to migration notes
    - known issues / exceptions
    - rollback plan owner + link to dashboards

[ ] #announcements post (customer-facing tone) prepared with PM:
    - emphasize reliability improvements + consistency
    - avoid alarming language about “retry storms”
    - point to how to configure timeouts/retries

[ ] Docs site deploy confirmed includes:
    - consistent option names and examples
    - streaming guide parity update


J) Known exceptions / TODOs (must be empty to ship stable; otherwise must be explicitly accepted)
- (none yet)


Appendix: quick reference defaults (fill in final numbers once ADR is locked)
Retries
- Retryable HTTP statuses: 408, 409, 429, 5xx (excluding 501?) per standard
- Network errors: connection reset, TLS handshake errors, DNS failures (best-effort per language)
- Max attempts: __
- Backoff: exponential with jitter; base __ ms; cap __ ms
- Retry-After: supported; both seconds and HTTP-date formats

Timeouts
- Default overall: __ ms
- If connect/read supported: connect __ ms, read __ ms (map to overall where not supported)

Streaming
- On disconnect after partial tokens: raise typed error including request_id + partial output accessible as per SDK design
- Automatic retry: default off once any tokens received; docs show safe pattern (idempotency keys)

Notes
- If we ship with different defaults in one language due to client limitations, it MUST be called out in migration notes and parity matrix.
